gnosh agents

  The sessions that run in the background, and those that ran: a view of them
  on a terminal. The sessions gnosh --bg, /background and /fork started, from
  every folder (with --cwd, from that folder and the folders in it): the
  working ones first, then those done in the last week. On a terminal it is a
  view to work in, as Claude Code's agent view: Space peeks at a run, Enter
  watches a working one or opens one that is over, Ctrl+X stops one, a prompt
  typed at the bottom starts one, and ? lists the keys; -y, --permission-mode,
  --model and --effort go to the runs it starts. Elsewhere, and with --json,
  it prints the list, each run named by the start of its ID, which gnosh logs,
  gnosh stop and gnosh -r take.

  Not built yet in this build of gnosh: typing it stops with a message that
  says so.

Usage
  gnosh agents [flags]

Flags
  --json
      Print JSON instead of text: the working sessions, and with --all the
      others too. (Not built yet.)
  --all
      Also list every session that is done, not only those of the last week.
      (Not built yet.)
  --cwd <dir>
      Work in this folder instead of the current one.
  -y, --yolo, --dangerously-skip-permissions
      Skip every permission question; the same as --permission-mode
      bypassPermissions. A print run refuses whatever would have asked, unless
      it is given this, a permission mode or allow rules.
  --permission-mode <mode>
      Start in this permission mode: default (also written manual), plan,
      acceptEdits, dontAsk or bypassPermissions. (Not built yet.)
  -m, --model <model>
      Use this model for this run only, written as model or provider/model.
      Nothing is saved.
  --reasoning-effort, --effort <level>
      How hard the model thinks in this run. The levels depend on the model.
      (Not built yet.)
  -h, --help
      Show help: gnosh's, or after a command's name that command's.
